extra.message: GET /api/import-export/export/tickets/:ticketId/rendered passes the unvalidated exportFormat query parameter into outputPath and this shell command. A team lead or administrator can supply shell metacharacters in exportFormat to execute arbitrary commands with the backend process's privileges.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: POST /api/webhooks/partner-sync/:payload decodes caller-controlled JSON and uses plainToClass without validation or an attribute allowlist. Every property except ticketId reaches Prisma's update data. An agent authorized for one ticket can modify protected fields and submit nested relation updates, including changing a related user's role or passwordHash. The initial ticket access check does not authorize these operations.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: The unauthenticated POST /api/auth/forgot-password endpoint returns the valid resetToken directly to whoever submits an existing user's email. The caller can immediately submit that token to /api/auth/reset-password and replace the victim's password, including an administrator's password. The testing comment is not enforced by an environment check.

cwe: CWE-640: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password

extra.message: JWT verification falls back to a publicly known signing key when JWT_SECRET is absent. auth.module.ts uses the same fallback for signing, including in production. An attacker can forge a bearer token whose sub identifies an existing active user; validate() then loads that user's database role, enabling impersonation and administrator access.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: Public registration assigns the new account to an existing organization solely by matching caller-supplied organizationName. No invitation, membership approval, or email-domain verification is required. An attacker can register using a victim organization's name and obtain organization-wide ticket, reply, and attachment access. initializeAccount repeats this behavior at lines 326–335.

cwe: CWE-863: Incorrect Authorization

extra.message: GET /api/tickets initially restricts customers to user.organizationId, but then overwrites that restriction with the organizationId query parameter. Any authenticated customer can supply another organization's ID and retrieve its tickets, including descriptions and requester contact information.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The support_agent/team_lead authorization branch applies no database restriction. GET /api/tickets therefore returns tickets across all teams, including descriptions and customer information, to ordinary agents. This bypasses the assignment/team restriction enforced by checkTicketAccess() on ticket details.

cwe: CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: GET /api/tickets/:id includes internalNotes and returns the complete ticket after checking only ticket access. Customers can consequently read staff-only notes and their authors' details for organization tickets. GET /api/tickets/:id/timeline independently exposes the same notes and internal audit records through the unconditional queries and response assembly at lines 948–985.

cwe: CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: checkSimpleAccess() checks customer organization membership but accepts every staff user without checking assignment or team. getReplies() and getTicketTimeline() use this helper, allowing agents to retrieve replies, internal notes, and audit history for tickets that the main detail endpoint denies. getInternalNotes() likewise checks only the staff role and ticket existence at lines 892–908.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: DELETE /api/attachments/:id permits support agents and team leads, but delete() checks only whether the attachment exists before deleting its file and database record. userId is used only for auditing; checkTicketAccess() is never called. An agent can delete another team's attachment by supplying its ID even when downloading that attachment is forbidden.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: POST /api/escalations is available to customers, but create() checks only ticket existence and whether an active escalation exists. It never verifies the caller's organization or ticket access. A customer can escalate another organization's ticket, change its status through lines 122–125, and receive the full foreign ticket through include: { ticket: true }.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: GET /api/escalations/:id accepts membershipTier directly from the query string. Setting membershipTier=partner_reviewer returns the escalation before the customer organization check, without verifying reviewer membership. Any authenticated customer can retrieve another organization's escalation and associated ticket details.

cwe: CWE-807: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision

extra.message: Escalation detail authorization checks only customer organization membership. An ordinary support agent can retrieve any escalation by ID, including its ticket description and requester information, despite findAll() limiting agents to escalations they requested or were assigned. getAssignmentBrief() also grants every staff user access at lines 347–353.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: POST /api/escalations/:id/partner-handoff falls back to jwt.decode() whenever signature or expiration verification fails and also permits the none algorithm. Authenticated staff can submit forged or expired reviewer claims. The service records the attacker-selected reviewerEmail as an admitted partner handoff in the audit log and returns the attacker-selected accessLevel without authenticating those claims.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: POST /api/import-export/import/escalation-resolutions allows team leads to update any escalation ID supplied in CSV. Row validation checks field types but never checks the ticket's managed team or caller assignment; userId is used only for auditing. A lead can resolve or reject another team's escalations, bypassing checkEscalationAccess() used by the normal status endpoint.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The category stored through ticket creation or update is joined directly into a filesystem path and read without checking containment in templatesDir. A staff caller can store a category containing ../ segments and request /api/reports/ticket/:ticketId/category-summary to retrieve readable .txt files outside the template directory. The appended .txt suffix limits the targeted filenames but does not prevent traversal.

cwe: CWE-23: Relative Path Traversal

extra.message: Public registration permits accounts without an organization. For such a customer, this condition leaves baseWhere empty, so GET /api/tickets/dashboard returns system-wide ticket counts, priorities, statuses, and overdue totals instead of restricting or rejecting the request.

cwe: CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: The customer-accessible attachment endpoint uses FileInterceptor without a file-size limit or configured storage, causing Multer to buffer the entire upload in memory. AttachmentsModule supplies no limits, and upload() subsequently writes the buffer without a size check. An authenticated caller can exhaust backend memory with oversized multipart uploads before ticket authorization runs, or exhaust disk space using an accessible ticket.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: The public POST /api/auth/initialize-account endpoint passes provisioningTier directly to bcrypt.hash() as its cost. The DTO checks only that it is an integer. An unauthenticated attacker can select a cost such as 31, causing exponentially expensive hashing and prolonged CPU exhaustion. Request-count throttling does not bound the work performed by each accepted request.

cwe: CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption

extra.message: Customer import generates account passwords using Math.random(), a non-cryptographic random generator, and stores their hashes as active login credentials. Contact import repeats this at lines 193–194. Password security consequently depends on a generator unsuitable for secrets, and truncating its base-36 output further limits entropy.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)

extra.message: POST /api/auth/change-password extracts newPassword as a primitive body field without DTO validation, and changePassword() hashes it without checking length. A valid old password therefore allows an empty or one-character replacement, bypassing the minimum length enforced during registration and reset. LoginDto also accepts an empty password string.

cwe: CWE-521: Weak Password Requirements

extra.message: Password reset updates passwordHash and removes only the reset token. Existing access tokens remain valid because JwtStrategy checks only signature, expiration, user existence, and isActive, with no password-change timestamp or token version. An attacker holding a stolen bearer token retains access after account recovery until its expiration, which defaults to 24 hours. changePassword() has the same omission.

cwe: CWE-613: Insufficient Session Expiration

extra.message: The public portal check-in accepts a ticket number and requester email as sufficient identity verification, without a password or proof of mailbox possession. It returns the ticket's subject, status, and internal ID. Ticket numbers are generated from only 100,000 possibilities in tickets.service.ts, so someone knowing a victim's email can enumerate matching tickets. The public resume endpoint uses the same check.

cwe: CWE-287: Improper Authentication

extra.message: Ticket export writes customer-controlled subjects, organization names, and user names to CSV without neutralizing formula prefixes. A customer can store a value beginning with = and have it interpreted as a spreadsheet formula when staff open the export. exportEscalations() similarly exports unescaped subjects, reasons, and names at lines 371–395. CSV quoting alone does not prevent formula interpretation.

cwe: CWE-1236: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File

extra.message: GET /api/knowledge-base/search accepts a customer-controlled query string and interpolates it directly into the server log. The DTO permits newline and control characters. A caller can inject additional log lines or terminal control sequences, forging search activity and corrupting log presentation.

cwe: CWE-117: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs

extra.message: GET /api/sla/forecast trusts the caller-supplied x-ops-context: internal-ops header to expose exception messages and stack traces. A team lead can trigger a Prisma validation error with an invalid date and receive internal query and filesystem details, including in production. The header is not authenticated as an internal operations identity.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
